messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: elevated 5xx rates observed for frontend-api (multiple services) in us-west-2a starting ~T-2m. Auto-signal threshold crossed. Paging oncall.sre
sre-jen: acked, joining. seeing surge in 502/503s in the gateway logs, lots of downstream timeouts.
eng-raj: grabbing traces. preliminary look shows a bunch of `failed SRV lookup` errors from internal service discovery when trying to reach service-backend-*. Logs:
```
ERROR service-discovery: lookup service-backend._tcp.prod.svc.cluster.local: no such host
WARN coredns: upstream response timeout after 5s
```
net-maya: are we seeing cloud resolver issues too? Any cross-region routing alerts from the cloud provider?
prod-support: customer impact: 6 active customer sessions affected, one enterprise reported real-time sync failures. Raising P1 support tickets for those customers.
sre-jen: running quick checks on K8s nodes in us-west-2a. `kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l k8s-app=kube-dns -o wide` shows coredns replicas on two nodes in the AZ, one in CrashLoopBackOff for ~30s.
eng-raj: reproducing SRV failure locally against cluster DNS: `dig +noall +answer SRV _grpc._tcp.service-backend.prod.svc.cluster.local @10.0.0.10` returns SERVFAIL intermittently.
net-maya: cloud provider status shows network flap in us-west-2a affecting internal routing between nodes and managed resolver endpoints. Filing a support case and linking.
incident-commander-dave: ok, this looks like internal DNS resolution failures caused by AZ networking instability impacting CoreDNS upstreams. Triage plan:
  - immediate: scale and restart CoreDNS in affected clusters to re-establish DNS cache and push queries to healthy upstreams
  - mitigate customer impact: flip traffic away from us-west-2a pods where possible (route to other AZs/regions), enable retry/backoff on client side where configured
  - communications: update status page and notify affected customers via prod-support
sre-jen: performing `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/coredns --context=prod-us-west-2a` now. increasing replicas from 2->4 to spread across nodes not in suspected AZ segment.
eng-raj: ran a quick curl against an unaffected replica in us-west-2b, SRV lookups succeed. After coredns rollout, I'm seeing resolution restored on ~40% of requests.
prod-support: posted initial incident note to status.redwood.example.com — holding on notifying enterprise contacts until we confirm mitigation.
net-maya: cloud case updated: internal router queueing and partial packet loss in us-west-2a. They are routing some control-plane traffic to alternate paths; ETA unknown.
eng-raj: as a temporary workaround, I pushed a node-local-dns DaemonSet to affected nodes so queries hit local caching resolver first. Config snippet:
```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata: name: node-local-dns
spec: template:
  spec:
    containers:
    - name: nodelocal
      image: k8s.gcr.io/k8s-dns-node-cache:1.16.2
      args: ["--localip","169.254.20.10","--upstream","10.3.0.2:53,10.3.0.3:53"]
```
sre-jen: node-local cache helped reduce SRV failures to near-zero for pods on those nodes. Shifting traffic away from the problematic AZ further improved client success rates.
incident-commander-dave: declaring Sev2 due to multiple customers and degraded platform-wide routing. Continue mitigation steps; make sure we capture timelines.
prod-support: notified 3 enterprise contacts (ACME, FinCo, MediaCorp) with current mitigation steps and ETA of 30-60m for stabilization.
cust-visibility-bot: posted customer-facing blurb to the incident page.
net-maya: cloud provider reported partial recovery in the AZ routing; they recommend draining affected hosts and reattaching to healthy subnets. gonna coordinate with infra to cordon and drain nodes.
sre-jen: cordoned 3 nodes in us-west-2a and drained them. `kubectl get pods -o wide` shows workloads moved to us-west-2b/2c.
eng-raj: after drains and restarts, SRV lookups are stable across the cluster for 15m. 5xx counts trending down to baseline.
prod-support: customers acknowledged follow-up messages, one customer reported some backlog delays but no data loss.
incident-commander-dave: good. prepare for handoff: my shift ends in 25m. who is taking night oncall?
sre-jen: I can take the handoff and remain the incident lead for the next shift. Notes:
  - root cause appears to be AZ-level networking flaps causing CoreDNS upstream timeouts and cache thrash
  - mitigations applied: coredns rollout, scaled replicas, node-local-dns daemonset, cordon/drain of affected nodes, traffic steering from router layer
  - next actions: collect CoreDNS logs, collect cloud routing logs, confirm provider RCA, add autoscaling/replica policy to tolerate single AZ failures, evaluate running node-local-dns across clusters permanently
sre-jen: handing over to night SRE; leaving runbook steps in the incident doc and pinned commands. (see pinned commands list)
incident-commander-dave: thanks. we'll keep monitoring for 2h and then transition to postmortem.
oncall-bot: NOTE: paging policy reminder sent to oncall.sre. :white_check_mark:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: stabilization observed, moving to monitoring state. Will mark closed when stable for 60m.
prod-support: closing external communications thread after confirming enterprise contacts got updates.
sre-jen: marking this thread for postmortem. Tags: DNS, CoreDNS, networking, AZ-us-west-2a, mitigation-node-local-dns
cust-visibility-bot: incident status: STABLE. final note posted to status page.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: timeline and mitigation recorded. Please file follow-up postmortem within 72h. :lock_with_key:
